shortDescription: Sahara: A Palliative Care Companion. Care notes and daily support for families.
fullDescription:
Sahara — A Palliative Care Companion

Keep goals-of-care conversations, daily care and useful information together for patients, families and care teams.

Keep the words that matter
Record a conversation with everyone's permission, dictate a speaker's turn on a supported phone, or type it. Review the original words, keep earlier note versions and share the exact version you discussed. In shared care, clinical review requires independent clinician approval and a separate patient invitation. Patient and family confirmations are recorded separately.

Follow daily care
Keep prescribed medicines, appointments, questions and tasks together. Add personal symptom notes with a 0–10 rating or an unrated response, the time, who answered and any words you want to keep. Compare entries with matching context and share them with your care team. The diary does not diagnose symptoms or calculate a clinical risk score. Optional Android reminders can be delayed by phone settings and are not an emergency service.

Find palliative care centres
Browse 1,631 published listings across 36 Indian states and union territories. Search the list, open a map, call a centre or get directions. Listings include dated sources and do not confirm current services or medicine stock. Call before travelling.

Keep and read your reports
Add PDFs or photos to Documents. Read printed English and Hindi text on your phone, compare it with the original and correct it before saving medicine details or copied facts. Original report files stay on the phone unless you choose to share a copy.

Optional Hindi and English tools
Transcribe a saved, consented recording locally with Qwen3-ASR after a separate 987 MB model download. This requires a supported 64-bit phone and sufficient free memory. There is no cloud speech fallback. Check names, numbers and mixed-language words against the recording before using the text.
Optional Hindi–English translation runs on your phone after a language-pack download. The original remains available. Machine translation is not a clinical interpretation.

Choose what you share
Basic records work without an account. Sign in to save care records and share permitted information with people you invite. Symptom notes saved in that account follow its sharing rules. Unsent phone drafts, recordings and original report files are not automatically uploaded. Text you explicitly save or send to shared care is stored with your account. There are no ads. Google ML Kit sends technical usage metrics and diagnostics as explained in the privacy policy.

Sahara is not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent a medical condition, recommend treatment or replace professional medical care. Ask a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice. Care notes record a discussion; they are not prescriptions or legal directives.

listingDraft.fullDescription:
Sahara: A Palliative Care Companion

For patients, families and doctors.

Keep the words that matter from a goals-of-care conversation. Type the conversation, record it with everyone's permission, or dictate one selected speaker's turn on a supported phone. Check the words and build the note from exact source excerpts. A doctor can review and save a version; the patient confirms first, then family can add separate confirmations of that same version. Names and roles are self-entered, not verified credentials or legal consent. Earlier versions and their original words remain available.

Ask the care team to talk, pick up a request and keep named tasks with acceptance and completion status. Plan visits, tests, procedures and follow-ups in a dated calendar. Enter numeric lab results with the report's units and printed ranges, and view values over time. Lab history does not interpret results or recommend treatment. Add prescribed medicines, check-ins, questions and daily notes. Medicine reminders are not available.

Documents keeps user-selected PDFs and photos together. Open a report or share a copy using Android. Report files and recordings remain private phone copies and do not sync to other devices. Saved recordings are not automatically transcribed. Read aloud uses an installed offline voice and does not translate. Live dictation requires an installed on-device recognition service; typing and recording remain available when it is unsupported.

Sign in to save care notes and daily entries to your account. Invite family or care team members to read them or allow changes. Conversation requests and tasks are shared records, not dispatched calls or email. Unfinished conversations are not uploaded.

Find listed palliative care centres in Karnataka on a MapLibre map or in the list. Call a centre or get directions. Directory entries do not confirm current medicine stock. There are no ads. Photo scanning is currently off; medicines can be entered manually.

Doctor login opens an isolated fictional preview for exploring scheduling and note review. Its sample records and marked preview PDFs are not verified clinical records or connected patient accounts.

This app is not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent a condition, recommend treatment or replace professional medical care. Ask a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice. Care notes record a discussion; they are not prescriptions or legal directives.

previousPublishedListing.fullDescription:
Sahara: A Palliative Care Companion

For patients, families and doctors.

Keep the words that matter from a goals-of-care conversation. A doctor can review the note and save a version. The patient or family can read and confirm that same version. Earlier notes and the original conversation stay available.

Record a conversation with everyone's permission, or type the words you want to keep. Add prescribed medicines, visits, questions, tasks and daily notes. Find listed palliative care centres in Karnataka, call them or get directions. Directory entries do not confirm current medicine stock.

Keep PDFs and photos together in Documents. Find a report by name, then open it or share a copy with your care team. Report files stay on your phone and are not synced to other devices.

Sign in to save care notes and daily entries to your account. Invite family or care team members to read them, or allow them to make changes. Recordings and unfinished conversations are not uploaded. Find centres on a MapLibre map or in the list. There are no ads. This version does not transcribe audio automatically, verify clinician identity or send medicine reminders.

This app is not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any medical condition, recommend treatment or replace professional medical care. Ask a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice. Care notes record a discussion; they are not prescriptions or legal directives.
previousPublishedListing.reviewInstructions: Use fictional data. More > Your account: sign in and add a person. Talk: type, link excerpts, Doctor review/save, Patient confirm, then Family confirm. Today: Care team, Calendar, Lab history. Doctor login is a separate fictional preview; roles are self-entered. Dictation and offline read aloud require installed services. Saved audio is not transcribed. Photo scanning, cloud audio and medicine reminders are off. Documents stay on this phone. No payment/OTP.

releaseNotes: Add personal symptom notes with ratings, context-matched comparisons and sharing. Browse 1,631 published care-centre listings across 36 states and union territories. Optional Hindi/English recording transcription runs on your phone after a 987 MB download. Read printed Hindi/English text, use offline translation and set care reminders. Shared clinical review requires independent clinician approval and a patient invitation. Check recognised words against the original.
